action: No action needed; for awareness. Organisations holding Washington residents' data: breaches affecting more than 500 residents must be reported to the Attorney General's Office.
date_note: Date of the Attorney General's news release; Insurance Journal covered the report on 19 November.
exec: Cyberattacks, with ransomware the most common method, were the leading cause of reported breaches in Washington state.
plain: Washington's attorney general reports 197 data breaches over one year, with more than 3.5 million notices sent to residents. Cyberattacks were the leading cause, and ransomware was the most common method.

key_findings: 197 data breaches were reported to the Washington AG's Office between July 24, 2025 and July 23, 2026, with more than 3.5 million notices sent to residents.
Cyberattacks were the leading cause with 139 incidents; ransomware was the most common method, responsible for 86 incidents.
Social Security numbers were exposed in 148 breaches, which the release describes as over 75% of all reported breaches.
No breach affecting 1 million or more Washington residents was reported, and both breach and notice counts declined from the previous reporting year.
recommendations: Expand the legal definition of personal information to include ITINs, Tribal identification and enrollment numbers, IRS Identity Protection PINs, precise geolocation data, and the last four digits of Social Security numbers combined with a name.
Require entities that own or license Washingtonians' personal information to maintain reasonable security procedures.
Require notification when an AI agent operated by an entity gains unauthorized access to a Washington resident's personal information.

sources.name: Washington Attorney General's Office news release

summary: The Washington Attorney General's annual Data Breach Report, announced in its 9 November release, counts 197 breaches reported to the state between July 24, 2025 and July 23, 2026, with more than 3.5 million notices to residents. Cyberattacks caused 139 incidents, 86 of them ransomware. The release says both counts fell from the previous reporting year.
title: Washington AG report: 197 data breaches and more than 3.5 million notices in the year to July 2026

validation.note: The Attorney General's news release was read; the full PDF report was not opened. Insurance Journal relays the same figures.
